items.title: A named decider and a written rule for a split panel
items.content:
# A named decider and a written rule for a split panel

Before the panel sits, one member is named as holding the decision and the rule for an even split is written down; when the split happens, the candidate is told that it did and which way the rule ran.

### Expected Effects
- mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse keeps operating — panels will split — but stops resolving by default and unrecorded
- The candidate learns the outcome turned on a tie rule, not on a finding about them

### Measurements
- `tie_rule_declared_rate`
- `impasse_disclosure_rate`
items.summary: Before the panel sits, one member is named as holding the decision and the rule for an even split is written down; when the split happens, the candidate is told that it did and which way the rule ran.
expected_effects: mech.hiring_manager_consensus_impasse keeps operating — panels will split — but stops resolving by default and unrecorded
The candidate learns the outcome turned on a tie rule, not on a finding about them

specimens.label: The rule, written before the panel meets

lines.text: Decider for req #5120: the hiring manager. On an even split the decider decides and records one paragraph of reasons.
Panel 2–2 on system design depth. Decider: no hire. Reason recorded: the two dissenting scores rested on the same unasked follow-up.
To the candidate: the panel did not reach agreement; the decision fell to the named decider under the rule set before the round.

specimens.reading: Panels split, and no rule stops them splitting. What a written rule stops is the split being resolved by whoever is most tired, and then reported outward as a considered judgement about the candidate. The default nobody wrote down is almost always no hire — which means the absence of a rule is itself a rule, and an unstated one.

perspectives.sees: A line to fill in before the panel is scheduled: who decides, and what happens on a tie.
perspectives.reads: The tie rule was always there — it was just never written, and unwritten it defaulted to the outcome that requires nobody to be responsible for it.
perspectives.does: Names the decider, writes the tie rule, and records a paragraph of reasons when the rule is used.

perspectives.sees: A debrief that ends with a recorded decision rather than a second round of scheduling.
perspectives.reads: An impasse used to cost the candidate weeks and produce nothing to send; now it produces a sentence that is true and can be sent the same day.
perspectives.does: Sends the outcome with the fact of the split in it, rather than converting it into a fit narrative.

perspectives.sees: An outcome that says the panel disagreed and a named person decided under a rule fixed beforehand.
perspectives.reads: Being split on is not the same as being found wanting: half the room was on the other side, and what settled it was a rule about ties.
perspectives.does: Reads the result as a close call rather than a verdict, and reapplies where the registry says the same team reopens.

items.title: Auto-Close Stale Job Requisitions
items.content:
# Auto-Close Stale Job Requisitions

Implement an automated ATS policy to expire public listings when headcount authorisation lapses or the configured interview-inactivity interval elapses.

### Expected Effects
- mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition stops operating: a listing cannot outlive the authorisation that funded it
- Silence after applying acquires a bound — the record is closed and the closure is sent

### Measurements
- `stale_requisition_rate`
- `closure_latency_days`
items.summary: Implement an automated ATS policy to expire public listings when headcount authorisation lapses or the configured interview-inactivity interval elapses.
expected_effects: mech.stale_or_orphaned_job_requisition stops operating: a listing cannot outlive the authorisation that funded it
Silence after applying acquires a bound — the record is closed and the closure is sent

specimens.label: The rule, and what it did

lines.text: Policy: expire_listing when headcount_authorisation lapses OR no interview activity for 45 days
req #4471 — last interview activity 47 days ago → listing withdrawn from careers page and aggregators
Candidates with applications in flight: 84 — each notified that the search has closed, with the date.

specimens.reading: The same batch job that produces silent bulk rejections can be pointed at the listing instead of the candidate. The cost is a configuration line.

perspectives.sees: A configuration line, and the count of open requisitions it would withdraw this quarter, on the same cycle where headcount is reviewed.
perspectives.reads: What is being spent is optionality: a listing that closes on a timer cannot be held open while funding is decided, and reopening it runs the approval chain again.
perspectives.does: Sets the interval and what counts as activity, and decides whether a lapsed authorisation withdraws the listing or only flags it for review.

perspectives.sees: Listings dropping off the careers page overnight, and the batch notification going to every application still in flight against them.
perspectives.reads: A requisition closed on a timer is counted as closed rather than filled, and the pipeline built against it is gone if the search restarts.
perspectives.does: Sends the closure notice with the date on it, and asks for the requisition to be reopened where the manager still intends to hire.

perspectives.sees: A message naming the requisition, the date the search closed, and the reason the listing came down.
perspectives.reads: The process ended for a reason that has nothing to do with the application; there is nothing further to wait for and nothing left to infer.
perspectives.does: Closes the file, stops holding capacity for a possible next round, and reapplies if the role is posted again.

perspectives.sees: A customer enabling an expiry rule pointed at the listing, on the same scheduler that already expires unreviewed applications.
perspectives.reads: This is an existing batch capability with a different target rather than new machinery; whether it runs is a customer setting.
perspectives.does: Ships the rule as a configurable option, and its default value decides how many customers ever run it.

items.title: Bench availability declared at each stage gate
items.content:
# Bench availability declared at each stage gate

At every advance the search states whether an already-employed engineer between projects could still take the seat, and an external candidate closed out by a bench fill is told so, with the date the availability appeared.

### Expected Effects
- mech.bench_priority_fill keeps operating — it cannot be removed — but stops being read as a verdict on the candidate
- External effort spent against an internally contestable seat becomes countable, and can be priced

### Measurements
- `bench_fill_closure_rate`
- `dated_closure_notice_rate`
items.summary: At every advance the search states whether an already-employed engineer between projects could still take the seat, and an external candidate closed out by a bench fill is told so, with the date the availability appeared.
expected_effects: mech.bench_priority_fill keeps operating — it cannot be removed — but stops being read as a verdict on the candidate
External effort spent against an internally contestable seat becomes countable, and can be priced

specimens.label: The notice that replaces the alignment letter

lines.text: Backend engineer, req #5120 — the search is closed and why
On 14 March an engineer already employed here came off a project that ended early and was assigned to this seat. The requisition is filled internally as of that date.
Your panel scored above the bar. Nothing in your assessment is the reason this ended, and the scores are held for 12 months against the next opening at this level.

specimens.reading: A company will always prefer an engineer it is already paying, and this does not ask it to stop. It asks the date to be named. The letter costs a paragraph and takes away the only thing the candidate would otherwise have to work with: an inference about their own performance drawn from an event that had nothing to do with it.

perspectives.sees: A field on the requisition recording whether an internal availability is live, and a closure code that distinguishes a bench fill from a hire and from a cancellation.
perspectives.reads: The distinction already exists in the staffing system; what is new is that it reaches the outside. A search that closes internally and is reported as a hire understates how often external effort is spent against a seat that was never contestable.
perspectives.does: Adds the closure code, and requires the date the availability appeared to be carried into the notice.

perspectives.sees: The staffing feed showing a bench engineer assigned to the requisition mid-search, and a pipeline that has to be closed out that day.
perspectives.reads: The close-out is not a judgement to be softened into alignment language — the reason is a date, and writing the date is faster than composing around it.
perspectives.does: Sends the dated notice to everyone still in flight, and records the assessment scores against the next opening rather than discarding them.

perspectives.sees: A dated reason: a seat filled from inside on a day that can be checked against the day the process went quiet.
perspectives.reads: The outcome was decided by an event in someone else's project schedule. There is no performance signal in it to act on, and no version of the interview that would have changed it.
perspectives.does: Stops re-reading the panel for a fault that was not there, and keeps the standing score rather than starting over.

items.title: Candidate ATS Parser Conformance Test Utility
items.content:
# Candidate ATS Parser Conformance Test Utility

Provide candidates with an open-source parsing validation tool to verify CV machine-readability before submission.

### Expected Effects
- The candidate can see the extraction before submitting, so an unreadable file is distinguishable from a thin one
- mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure moves from invisible to checkable on the candidate's side of the line

### Measurements
- `parser_extraction_error_rate`
- `ingestion_pass_rate`
items.summary: Provide candidates with an open-source parsing validation tool to verify CV machine-readability before submission.
expected_effects: The candidate can see the extraction before submitting, so an unreadable file is distinguishable from a thin one
mech.ats_parser_extraction_failure moves from invisible to checkable on the candidate's side of the line

specimens.label: Tool output, before submitting
specimens.subject: hoba-parse-check · cv.pdf

lines.text: Extraction score: 41/100
Work experience entries recovered: 0 of 5 — two-column layout detected
Skills recovered: 0 of 24 — rendered inside a graphic
Suggested: single-column export, text-based headings, skills as plain text.
Re-check after changes: extraction score 93/100, 5 of 5 entries, 24 of 24 skills.

specimens.reading: This is a candidate-side intervention. Seeing what the parser sees turns an invisible failure into a fixable file.

perspectives.sees: An extraction report against their own file: how many work entries and skills a parser recovers, and which layout choice dropped them.
perspectives.reads: The failure was in the document rather than in the record, and it is fixable before submission rather than inferable afterwards.
perspectives.does: Re-exports single-column with text headings, re-checks, and submits the version that survives extraction.

perspectives.sees: A complete profile in the queue: work history in fields, skills in fields, orderable against the rest.
perspectives.reads: A profile with nothing in the experience field and a profile whose experience did not extract read identically from here; this removes one of the two before it arrives.
perspectives.does: Screens on the content, and in the applications that still arrive empty, an unreadable file and a thin record remain indistinguishable.

items.title: Candidate Work Index Submitted With the Application
items.content:
# Candidate Work Index Submitted With the Application

Submit a one-page index naming each work artefact, the part of it that is the candidate's and the direct path to it, and open that index in the first minutes of the live screen.

### Expected Effects
- mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation loses its default: the surface opened is the one the candidate named, with the part that is theirs stated on it
- A contribution held under another organisation arrives as a commit range rather than as something to be discovered
- The index travels with the application, so bar.inbound_screening_triage and bar.technical_screen_live_assessment open the same named artefacts instead of whatever a profile page shows first

### Measurements
- `work_index_attachment_rate`
- `named_artifact_citation_rate`
- `technical_screen_advance_rate`
items.summary: Submit a one-page index naming each work artefact, the part of it that is the candidate's and the direct path to it, and open that index in the first minutes of the live screen.
expected_effects: mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation loses its default: the surface opened is the one the candidate named, with the part that is theirs stated on it
A contribution held under another organisation arrives as a commit range rather than as something to be discovered
The index travels with the application, so bar.inbound_screening_triage and bar.technical_screen_live_assessment open the same named artefacts instead of whatever a profile page shows first

specimens.label: The one-page index, submitted with the application
specimens.subject: Work index — backend: storage and ingest

lines.text: Ingest library, upstream project under a different organisation. Mine: the storage layer rewrite — 40 commits, March to November. The link goes to the commit range, not to the account.
Internal service, not public. What can be shown: the design note with the employer's name removed, and a walkthrough on request.
Five-minute read path: the migration note in /docs, then the fourth commit in the range.
The CV line reads 'storage layer rewrite, upstream ingest library, contributor', so the claim and the path to it sit in one sentence.

specimens.reading: The surface a screener opens is a choice, and the default is a profile page in date order. The index makes that choice, and names which part of each artefact is the candidate's.

perspectives.sees: The surface an application opens on by default — a profile page, a list of repositories in date order — and their own work spread across it in a shape that page does not show.
perspectives.reads: Which surface is opened is decided by what the application carries, and the index is the part of that the candidate writes.
perspectives.does: Names each artefact, the part of it that is theirs and the direct path to it, and opens the index in the first minutes of the live screen instead of leaving the choice of surface to the hour.

perspectives.sees: An index in the application with named artefacts and direct links, alongside the profile link.
perspectives.reads: The minutes available per application go to something already located, and a line in the CV has a path attached that opens in one click.
perspectives.does: Records the note from the named artefact where the index points to one, and from the profile page where the application carries no index.

perspectives.sees: The index in the material the panel receives, with the ownership line and the read path in it.
perspectives.reads: The exercise hour and the evidence of past work stop competing for the same minutes: what to open is stated, so the round is spent on the exercise.
perspectives.does: Reads the named artefact before the session where it is short enough, and asks about that work in the round rather than about the profile.

items.title: Contractable jurisdictions listed in the posting
items.content:
# Contractable jurisdictions listed in the posting

The posting names the countries in which the employer can actually issue a contract — through an entity, an employer of record, or a contractor arrangement — so a constraint that no interview can change is known before the first call.

### Expected Effects
- mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint stops being discovered at the offer stage
- A lawful contracting limit becomes distinguishable from a ground that is not one

### Measurements
- `jurisdiction_list_published_rate`
- `late_stage_jurisdiction_rejection_rate`
items.summary: The posting names the countries in which the employer can actually issue a contract — through an entity, an employer of record, or a contractor arrangement — so a constraint that no interview can change is known before the first call.
expected_effects: mech.location_or_timezone_compliance_constraint stops being discovered at the offer stage
A lawful contracting limit becomes distinguishable from a ground that is not one

specimens.label: The line that goes where "remote" used to be

lines.text: Remote. Contract can be issued in: PL, UA, PT, DE (own entity); ES, RO (employer of record). Nowhere else, including as a contractor.
Overlap required with CET 10:00–15:00. This is a scheduling requirement, not a residence one.
This list is a statement about where we can contract, not about who may work: it is reviewed quarterly and dated below.

specimens.reading: A jurisdiction the employer cannot contract in is a real and lawful constraint, and it is also the one most often discovered at the offer stage. Published, it costs a line. Withheld, it spends the candidate's whole process — and it is indistinguishable from the ground that is not lawful, which is exactly why it has to be stated as a contracting fact with a date on it rather than as a preference about people.

perspectives.sees: The list finance and legal already hold — entities, employer-of-record coverage, and where contracting was declined — rendered into the posting template.
perspectives.reads: Publishing it converts a constraint that currently surfaces as a late rejection into one the market routes around, and it separates a contracting fact from a ground that would not be lawful.
perspectives.does: Publishes the jurisdiction list with a review date, and keeps timezone overlap stated separately from residence.

perspectives.sees: A published list to screen against, instead of a question that has to be asked carefully on the first call.
perspectives.reads: The conversation that used to end a process at week six now does not start one, and the reason given is a fact about the employer rather than about the candidate.
perspectives.does: Points candidates outside the list at the roles that can contract where they live, and stops running processes that cannot end in a contract.

perspectives.sees: A named list of countries and a separate, stated overlap window.
perspectives.reads: Whether this role can exist for them is answered before any effort is spent, and a rejection on this ground later would now be checkable against a published statement.
perspectives.does: Applies where a contract is possible, and treats the overlap window as the negotiable part that it is.

items.title: Critique injected on script in the collaborative exercise
items.content:
# Critique injected on script in the collaborative exercise

The collaborative round carries a written script: the same objection is raised at the same point for every candidate, and the panel records what was said in response rather than how the room felt.

### Expected Effects
- mech.communication_or_working_style_friction is measured against a common prompt rather than inferred from an interviewer's chosen one
- Interviewer variance stops entering the verdict as if it were candidate behaviour

### Measurements
- `scripted_prompt_coverage`
- `panel_inter_rater_agreement`
items.summary: The collaborative round carries a written script: the same objection is raised at the same point for every candidate, and the panel records what was said in response rather than how the room felt.
expected_effects: mech.communication_or_working_style_friction is measured against a common prompt rather than inferred from an interviewer's chosen one
Interviewer variance stops entering the verdict as if it were candidate behaviour

specimens.label: The script, and the line it produces

lines.text: Scripted at minute 18, verbatim for every candidate: "I think this design is wrong — you have put the queue in the wrong place."
Recorded: asked which failure the objection was about; restated the trade-off; proposed moving it and named what that would cost.
Not recorded: tone, warmth, whether the room enjoyed it. The rubric has no column for it, so no column carries it.

specimens.reading: Friction in a collaborative exercise is a real signal, and this does not deny it — it makes it comparable. Unscripted, the objection arrives when an interviewer happens to feel like raising it, in words chosen for that candidate, and what comes back is scored against a memory of how other rounds went. Scripted, the same prompt produces answers that can be set side by side.

perspectives.sees: A one-page script with the objection, the minute it lands, and the three things the answer is scored on.
perspectives.reads: What the panel disagreed about was never the candidate — it was which objection each interviewer raised and how hard. Fixing the prompt leaves only the answer to disagree about.
perspectives.does: Writes the script once per role, and holds the panel to scoring the response rather than the room.

perspectives.sees: An objection that arrives as part of the exercise, and a rubric that names what the answer is being read for.
perspectives.reads: The pushback is the test, not a reaction to something already gone wrong — so it can be answered on the merits instead of managed.
perspectives.does: Answers the objection rather than reading the room for what caused it.

perspectives.sees: Panel write-ups that name a scripted moment and quote the response, instead of arriving as impressions.
perspectives.reads: A write-up quoting a common prompt is the only kind that can be compared between candidates or defended after the fact.
perspectives.does: Returns the quoted exchange as the feedback, and refuses write-ups that score the room.

items.title: Dated Funding Certification Before the Final Round
items.content:
# Dated Funding Certification Before the Final Round

Carry a funding-certified-through date on every requisition, refuse to schedule a final round unless that date covers the expected start, and release the countersignature on a live certification rather than on a second approval.

### Expected Effects
- bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval is passed before the final round is scheduled: the certification date is in the requisition before the panel sits, rather than after it recommends
- mech.headcount_freeze_or_budget_cancellation meets a requisition whose funded-through date is either live or lapsed; where a freeze lands mid-loop the requisition changes to a dated state and every candidate in flight is written to on that date
- bar.offer_closing_contract_execution stops carrying a funding decision: the countersignature is blocked while the certification has lapsed and released while it is live

### Measurements
- `panel_to_offer_latency_days`
- `requisition_funding_lapse_rate`
- `countersignature_latency_days`
items.summary: Carry a funding-certified-through date on every requisition, refuse to schedule a final round unless that date covers the expected start, and release the countersignature on a live certification rather than on a second approval.
expected_effects: bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval is passed before the final round is scheduled: the certification date is in the requisition before the panel sits, rather than after it recommends

mech.headcount_freeze_or_budget_cancellation meets a requisition whose funded-through date is either live or lapsed; where a freeze lands mid-loop the requisition changes to a dated state and every candidate in flight is written to on that date
bar.offer_closing_contract_execution stops carrying a funding decision: the countersignature is blocked while the certification has lapsed and released while it is live

specimens.label: The requisition, with the funding date in it
specimens.subject: req #5120 · Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: funding_certified_through: 30 November · certified by finance 12 August
Final round requested — the scheduler reads the field: the certified date covers the expected start date. Round booked.
Scheduling message to the candidate: this requisition is funded through 30 November, and that is the date the approval behind it expires.
Contract issued · countersignature released on a live certification, with no second approval step.
Where a division freeze revokes the certification: req #5120 flips to a dated paused state and every candidate in flight is written to on that date.

specimens.reading: The date is one field. What it does is move the approval from after the panel to before the scheduler, and give the recruiter a date to quote where the pending row had none.

perspectives.sees: A certification with an expiry on every requisition, and a quarterly review in which each line already carries the date it runs out.
perspectives.reads: Optionality narrows: a requisition can no longer sit in pending while the quarter is decided, because pending now blocks the scheduler rather than the offer.
perspectives.does: Sets the certification horizon and who may re-certify, and decides whether a lapsed date pauses the requisition or closes it.

perspectives.sees: The funded-through date as a field in the requisition, and a scheduler that refuses a final round when the date does not cover the expected start.
perspectives.reads: A date exists to quote where the pending row had none; the cost is that some final rounds cannot be booked at all.
perspectives.does: Quotes the date when scheduling, and where the certification lapses mid-loop, sends the dated notice instead of waiting for the row to move.

perspectives.sees: A scheduling message naming the date the funding behind the requisition expires, and, where it lapses, a dated notice saying paused or closed.
perspectives.reads: The interval after a panel that went well has a stated cause and a boundary: the wait turns on a certification date rather than on the rounds already completed.
perspectives.does: Weighs that date against the other processes in flight, and stops holding capacity for this one once the notice says closed.

items.title: Disqualifying criteria published with the posting
items.content:
# Disqualifying criteria published with the posting

Every criterion the automated filter can reject on — a required acronym, a named certification, a years-of-experience threshold — is listed in the posting as a disqualifier, so a deterministic gate is legible before the application is written.

### Expected Effects
- mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter stops operating unseen: the rule that rejects is the rule that was published
- An application withheld against a stated disqualifier costs neither side a review

### Measurements
- `knockout_criteria_published_rate`
- `applications_per_opening`
items.summary: Every criterion the automated filter can reject on — a required acronym, a named certification, a years-of-experience threshold — is listed in the posting as a disqualifier, so a deterministic gate is legible before the application is written.
expected_effects: mech.automated_keyword_qualification_filter stops operating unseen: the rule that rejects is the rule that was published
An application withheld against a stated disqualifier costs neither side a review

specimens.label: The block that goes above the requirements

lines.text: Filtered automatically. An application is not read if it lacks any of: the string "Kubernetes" or "K8s"; 5+ years dated employment in backend engineering; work authorisation in DE, PL or UA.
Everything below this line is read by a person and weighed. Nothing below it rejects on its own.
If the tooling you used is called something else, write both names. The filter matches the string, not the work.

specimens.reading: The filter is not being removed — it is being published. What changes is who can see it: a rule that rejects on an exact string costs nothing to state, and stating it turns a silent rejection into a decision the candidate makes before spending the hour.

perspectives.sees: The knock-out rules already configured in the ATS, written out as a list, and the count of applications each one rejected last quarter.
perspectives.reads: The list is a description of the filter as it actually runs, not of the role as it was imagined — and a rule nobody is willing to publish is a rule that will not survive being read.
perspectives.does: Publishes the knock-out list, and strikes the rules that cannot be justified once they are written next to the work.

perspectives.sees: A short block naming exactly what will reject the application without a person reading it.
perspectives.reads: The gate is a string match, and a rejection against it says nothing about the work — it can be cleared by naming the same tool by both its names, or it cannot be cleared at all, and either way that is known now.
perspectives.does: Applies against a gate it can see, or does not, and stops reading a filter rejection as a verdict on the work.

perspectives.sees: Customers asking for the configured knock-out rules to be rendered into the posting template automatically.
perspectives.reads: The rules are already structured data in the requisition; rendering them is a template change, not a product, and the reason they were never shown is that nothing asked.
perspectives.does: Renders the knock-out block from the requisition config, so the published list cannot drift from the filter that runs.

items.title: Distinct Closure Status for Unreviewed Applications
items.content:
# Distinct Closure Status for Unreviewed Applications

Give the ATS a terminal status for an application closed without a human opening it, distinct from the one used for a reviewed decline, bind it into the notification template, and count it on the requisition.

### Expected Effects
- mech.automated_application_expiration_timeout can no longer write the value used for a decision: the expiry job writes closed_unreviewed, and the notification template carries that status
- The gap mech.recruiter_volume_quota_incentive_distortion runs on becomes a figure on the requisition — applications closed unopened are counted where applications received already are
- bar.inbound_screening_triage leaves a state that can be read from outside: not reached, reviewed and not advanced, or closed with the search

### Measurements
- `unreviewed_at_close_rate`
- `time_to_first_human_open_days`
- `closure_status_coverage`
items.summary: Give the ATS a terminal status for an application closed without a human opening it, distinct from the one used for a reviewed decline, bind it into the notification template, and count it on the requisition.
expected_effects: mech.automated_application_expiration_timeout can no longer write the value used for a decision: the expiry job writes closed_unreviewed, and the notification template carries that status
The gap mech.recruiter_volume_quota_incentive_distortion runs on becomes a figure on the requisition — applications closed unopened are counted where applications received already are
bar.inbound_screening_triage leaves a state that can be read from outside: not reached, reviewed and not advanced, or closed with the search

specimens.label: The status the batch writes, and where the count lands
specimens.subject: Requisition #4471 — queue closure

lines.text: Terminal statuses: reviewed_advanced · reviewed_declined · closed_unreviewed · closed_with_requisition. A record does not leave the queue without one of them.
Scheduled job expire_stale_applications — 312 matched; human_open recorded on 0 → status closed_unreviewed
Notice sent, status bound into the template: "Your application was not reviewed before this search closed. No assessment of your profile was made."
Requisition #4471 — received 640 · opened 219 · closed unreviewed 421

specimens.reading: The batch is the same batch. What changed is that the status it writes separates a record nobody opened from one that was declined, and the count of the first sits on the same dashboard as applications received.

perspectives.sees: A status vocabulary in which every way a record leaves the queue has its own terminal value, and the migration that splits the existing Rejected in two.
perspectives.reads: The split is a schema change and a template variable; what it exposes — how much of the queue was never opened — becomes a figure in every customer's dashboard.
perspectives.does: Ships the statuses and the counter, makes the terminal status a required variable in the notification template, and carries the customers whose reporting was built on a single Rejected value.

perspectives.sees: The requisition dashboard carrying received, opened and closed-unreviewed side by side, and the expiry batch landing in the third column.
perspectives.reads: How far the queue ran past the week is a published figure on the requisition rather than a condition of the job. Time-to-fill is still what the report is read for.
perspectives.does: Works the current inbound with the count standing next to it; where the count is argued about, it is argued about against the recruiting headcount that fixes review capacity.

perspectives.sees: A notice naming the status the record ended in, and whether a person opened it.
perspectives.reads: A record nobody reached and a record that was assessed and declined no longer arrive in the same words; only one of the two says anything about the profile.
perspectives.does: Reads the message for the status rather than for an assessment it states is not there, and decides about reapplying on that.

items.title: Domain requirement carries a stated ramp time
items.content:
# Domain requirement carries a stated ramp time

A requisition that asks for experience in one named vertical must state how long the team believes that domain takes to learn; where the answer is weeks, the requirement is scored as a preference rather than a gate.

### Expected Effects
- mech.domain_specificity_over_weighting must state its own cost before it can reject
- A requirement assembled from something other than the work becomes visible at the point it is written

### Measurements
- `ramp_estimate_completion_rate`
- `domain_only_rejection_rate`
items.summary: A requisition that asks for experience in one named vertical must state how long the team believes that domain takes to learn; where the answer is weeks, the requirement is scored as a preference rather than a gate.
expected_effects: mech.domain_specificity_over_weighting must state its own cost before it can reject
A requirement assembled from something other than the work becomes visible at the point it is written

specimens.label: The field the requisition gains

lines.text: Domain: payments. Ramp estimate entered by hiring manager: 6 weeks to first independent change.
Ramp ≤ 12 weeks → scored as preference. Screening may not reject on domain alone.
To make it a gate, name the regulation, certification or customer commitment that cannot wait 6 weeks.

specimens.reading: The manager is not asked to drop the preference — they are asked to price it. A vertical that takes six weeks to learn cannot also be the thing that disqualifies someone with ten years of the underlying systems work, and writing the estimate is what makes the two claims meet.

perspectives.sees: A required field asking how long the domain takes, next to the requirement that names it.
perspectives.reads: The estimate is one the team already makes when it onboards internal transfers; writing it down is what stops the same domain being treated as unlearnable for outsiders.
perspectives.does: Enters the estimate, and either justifies the gate or accepts candidates who clear everything except the vertical.

perspectives.sees: A screening rule that says which requirements may reject and which may only rank.
perspectives.reads: The instruction that used to arrive as "must have fintech" now arrives with a duration attached, and a duration can be argued with where a preference could not.
perspectives.does: Advances candidates strong on transferable depth where the ramp is short, and cites the estimate when the manager objects.

perspectives.sees: A posting that says how long the team thinks its domain takes to pick up.
perspectives.reads: Whether the vertical is a wall or a ramp is now the employer's stated position rather than something to guess at from a rejection.
perspectives.does: Applies to the roles where the ramp is stated and short, and stops rewriting a CV to fake a vertical.

items.title: Internal Candidacy Stated in the Posting
items.content:
# Internal Candidacy Stated in the Posting

Where a formal internal candidacy exists against a requisition at the moment it is published, the posting says so and says what the external loop decides.

### Expected Effects
- mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate stops being opaque at the gate it operates at: the composition of the slate is stated where the posting is, not at minute 41 of a final round
- bar.requisition_approval_public_posting publishes one more field — whether the external loop runs against an internal candidacy already formally under consideration

### Measurements
- `slate_disclosure_rate`
- `internal_fill_rate_on_posted_requisitions`
- `external_rounds_per_internal_fill`
items.summary: Where a formal internal candidacy exists against a requisition at the moment it is published, the posting says so and says what the external loop decides.
expected_effects: mech.pre_selected_internal_candidate stops being opaque at the gate it operates at: the composition of the slate is stated where the posting is, not at minute 41 of a final round
bar.requisition_approval_public_posting publishes one more field — whether the external loop runs against an internal candidacy already formally under consideration

specimens.label: The posting, with the slate in it
specimens.subject: Staff Engineer · Platform — status of the search

lines.text: Requisition 4820, approved, level L5. One internal candidate has been under formal consideration since 2 March.
The external loop runs to four rounds and the decision compares the slate; it is neither a formality nor a search with no incumbent.
If the internal candidacy is withdrawn, this line comes off and the posting is dated again.

specimens.reading: Nothing in the process changed. What changed is when the fact is available: on the posting, rather than as an aside in the last round.

perspectives.sees: A posting rule that applies to every requisition, and a proposed field stating what already stands behind one before it goes live.
perspectives.reads: A published slate makes an internal candidacy visible to that employee's own team and to everyone who reads the posting; a rule that discloses for all requisitions cannot be switched off for one.
perspectives.does: Defines when a candidacy counts as formal and therefore disclosable, and that definition is what the posting field is filled from.

perspectives.sees: Fewer external applications against a requisition carrying the line, and the same number of interview slots to fill.
perspectives.reads: The comparison the loop exists for still needs a slate; a smaller external pool is the cost of the pool knowing what it is entering.
perspectives.does: Runs the loop as posted, and where the external pool thins below what a comparison needs, asks whether the role should be posted externally at all.

perspectives.sees: A posting stating that an internal candidacy exists, with a date on it, before any round is scheduled.
perspectives.reads: The composition of the slate is stated rather than inferred, and the hours a four-round loop costs are weighed against it.
perspectives.does: Applies or does not, and where they do, asks at the first screen what the internal candidate has already been observed doing.

items.title: Interview Seats Booked With Prep Time and a Second Name on the Rota
items.content:
# Interview Seats Booked With Prep Time and a Second Name on the Rota

Book every interview seat as preparation plus session, take those hours off the sprint board, and give each round a second name on a standing rota so an unavailable interviewer passes the seat rather than moves the date.

### Expected Effects
- mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation loses one of its two outputs: a seat that cannot be filled moves the seat, not the date
- A round at bar.technical_screen_live_assessment is booked with reading time attached to it, so the material is opened before the session or the seat passes to the second name
- Interviewer hours sit on the sprint board as committed work rather than as an overrun absorbed by whoever had the slot

### Measurements
- `interview_reschedule_rate`
- `panel_seat_backfill_rate`
- `rounds_per_interviewer_month`
items.summary: Book every interview seat as preparation plus session, take those hours off the sprint board, and give each round a second name on a standing rota so an unavailable interviewer passes the seat rather than moves the date.
expected_effects: mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation loses one of its two outputs: a seat that cannot be filled moves the seat, not the date
A round at bar.technical_screen_live_assessment is booked with reading time attached to it, so the material is opened before the session or the seat passes to the second name
Interviewer hours sit on the sprint board as committed work rather than as an overrun absorbed by whoever had the slot

specimens.label: The same Wednesday, with a second name already on the round
specimens.subject: Technical screen — Thursday

lines.speaker: Engineering manager
lines.text: Thursday's screen needs a seat. You are on the rota this sprint, and the board is already two points lighter for it.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: I am on release duty. If I take it, it is a cold read.

lines.speaker: Engineering manager
lines.text: Then it goes to the second name on the rota — the prep block is on that calendar at 09:00 and the material is already there.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: Candidate told the same day: same slot, different interviewer, date unchanged.

specimens.reading: The release duty is still there. What changes is that the round carries a second name before the week starts, so an unavailable interviewer passes the seat instead of moving the date.

perspectives.sees: A rota with two names against each round of the sprint, and a sprint board with those hours already taken out of it.
perspectives.reads: Interview capacity is planned before the week rather than found inside it, and the cost is visible on the board where it was previously absorbed by whoever had the slot.
perspectives.does: Takes the points off the sprint for the rota week, and passes the seat to the second name when the first is on release duty.

perspectives.sees: A round that keeps its date, and an interviewer who opens the submitted work before the call rather than during it.
perspectives.reads: A change of interviewer arrives with the date unchanged, which is a different event from a round being moved.
perspectives.does: Keeps the slot and prepares once, instead of replanning the week around a moved round.

perspectives.sees: Panel seats coming back filled from the rota, and a reschedule request only where both names are unavailable.
perspectives.reads: A date that moves becomes the exception the process reports rather than the ordinary way a seat gets filled.
perspectives.does: Sends the invitation with the interviewer's name and the prep block already accepted, and names a new date only when both rota names are out.

items.title: Outreach States the Requisition Behind It
items.content:
# Outreach States the Requisition Behind It

Every outbound message names the requisition it is sent against and its state — approved and open, or a pool record against a forecast — and the pool records opened against a forecast are answered on the day planning decides it.

### Expected Effects
- bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact's pass condition is stated in the first message: whether a reply attaches to an authorised requisition or to a pool is part of what is sent
- mech.speculative_sourcing_talent_pooling_without_opening becomes datable — a conversation held against an unapproved forecast carries the planning date it depends on
- The silence after a speculative conversation acquires a bound: the planning decision goes to the records opened against that forecast

### Measurements
- `unattached_outreach_rate`
- `pool_record_age_days`
- `planning_decision_notice_rate`
items.summary: Every outbound message names the requisition it is sent against and its state — approved and open, or a pool record against a forecast — and the pool records opened against a forecast are answered on the day planning decides it.
expected_effects: bar.outbound_sourcing_talent_pool_contact's pass condition is stated in the first message: whether a reply attaches to an authorised requisition or to a pool is part of what is sent
mech.speculative_sourcing_talent_pooling_without_opening becomes datable — a conversation held against an unapproved forecast carries the planning date it depends on
The silence after a speculative conversation acquires a bound: the planning decision goes to the records opened against that forecast

specimens.label: The first message, and what it was attached to
specimens.subject: Two outreach templates, one week apart

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Req 5512, approved, open since 4 May, level L4. This is sent against that requisition — if you reply, that is the process you enter.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: No requisition yet. This is a pool record against a Q3 forecast; planning decides on 12 September and you get the outcome either way.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood — the second one I will answer in September.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Planning outcome: the forecast moved to Q1. The pool record is closed and I am not holding it open.

specimens.reading: Two templates instead of one. Whoever reads either of them knows which of the two conversations they are in before spending anything on it.

perspectives.sees: Two outreach templates in the sequencer, and the field on the contact record that decides which one goes out.
perspectives.reads: The reply rate on the pool template is not the reply rate on the requisition template, and both are counted against the same outreach target.
perspectives.does: Sends the template the record's state selects, and books the planning date as the day the pool records opened against that forecast are answered.

perspectives.sees: A first message that says which of the two it is, with a requisition number on it or a planning date.
perspectives.reads: A conversation against a forecast and a live process are separable before answering, and the silence that follows a deferred forecast has a date on it.
perspectives.does: Answers both, and schedules rounds against the one with a requisition behind it.

perspectives.sees: Outreach going out under a template that names the approval state of headcount the approval cycle has not decided.
perspectives.reads: A forecast named outside the company is a planning signal leaving the approval cycle before that cycle has settled anything.
perspectives.does: Decides which forecasts may be named in outreach and which may only be described as a pool, and that decision is the boundary the templates are written inside.

items.title: Publish the Technical Screen's Columns and Threshold Before the Round
items.content:
# Publish the Technical Screen's Columns and Threshold Before the Round

Publish the columns, their weights and the advancing threshold of the live technical screen alongside the posting, and score the round on those columns.

### Expected Effects
- bar.technical_screen_live_assessment's instrument exists before the hour it scores: the columns, the weights and the line are readable from outside the panel
- A total one point under the threshold at bar.technical_screen_live_assessment is locatable, because the number it is compared with is published
- A round read cold under mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation is scored on the published columns rather than on what the hour left as an impression

### Measurements
- `rubric_completion_rate`
- `borderline_outcome_rate`
items.summary: Publish the columns, their weights and the advancing threshold of the live technical screen alongside the posting, and score the round on those columns.
expected_effects: bar.technical_screen_live_assessment's instrument exists before the hour it scores: the columns, the weights and the line are readable from outside the panel
A total one point under the threshold at bar.technical_screen_live_assessment is locatable, because the number it is compared with is published
A round read cold under mech.interview_resource_scheduling_saturation is scored on the published columns rather than on what the hour left as an impression

specimens.label: The scoring instrument, published with the role
specimens.subject: Technical screen — how this hour is scored

lines.text: Correctness · complexity reasoning · communication · testing instinct. Each 0–5, equal weight.
14 of 20 advances. The columns and the line are fixed before the round and dated on this page.
One implementation task in a shared editor, 45 minutes, run by an engineer from the team the role sits in.
The four column scores are sent with the outcome, whichever way it goes.

specimens.reading: The gate was already a sum against a line. Publishing does not move the line; it puts the columns and the line on the side of the table where the hour is spent.

perspectives.sees: A page attached to every technical posting carrying four columns, their weights and the number a total is compared with.
perspectives.reads: A published instrument is one every panel has to score against and one the organisation is answerable to; the columns can no longer be settled after the round.
perspectives.does: Defines which instruments may be published and how a change to one is dated, and holds the publication back for roles where no rubric has been written.

perspectives.sees: The columns, the weights and the threshold before booking the hour, and the column scores with the outcome.
perspectives.reads: The hour is scored on four named things, so preparation has a target, and a total a point under the line reads as that rather than as a verdict on the person.
perspectives.does: Prepares against the named columns, and where the exercise format does not match what the role does, decides that before spending the hour.

perspectives.sees: The team's rubric as an external document with a date on it, and every panel entry now recorded against those columns.
perspectives.reads: The instrument is fixed before the round, so two interviewers disagreeing becomes a difference in a named column rather than a difference in what was being looked for.
perspectives.does: Writes the columns and the threshold down before the role opens, and takes a change to them through the same publication step rather than mid-search.

items.title: Recorded Finalist Standing With a Dated Re-Entry Route
items.content:
# Recorded Finalist Standing With a Dated Re-Entry Route

Record, for every finalist who cleared the bar and received no offer, the cohort size, the class of reason and a dated stage the record re-enters at when a requisition at the same level opens.

### Expected Effects
- mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort becomes a recorded outcome: the cohort size and the class of reason sit in the record and in what is sent, instead of arriving as a decline with no account of the group
- bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval: a requisition that closes with more finalists than offers leaves standings behind it that outlast the closing
- pat.closed_then_reposted_requisition_motif: a reposted requisition matches against the standings recorded against its previous run, and the stage a matched record re-enters at is stated

### Measurements
- `finalist_standing_record_rate`
- `finalist_reentry_rate`
- `reposted_requisition_match_rate`
items.summary: Record, for every finalist who cleared the bar and received no offer, the cohort size, the class of reason and a dated stage the record re-enters at when a requisition at the same level opens.
expected_effects: mech.stronger_competing_candidate_in_final_cohort becomes a recorded outcome: the cohort size and the class of reason sit in the record and in what is sent, instead of arriving as a decline with no account of the group
bar.headcount_executive_budget_approval: a requisition that closes with more finalists than offers leaves standings behind it that outlast the closing
pat.closed_then_reposted_requisition_motif: a reposted requisition matches against the standings recorded against its previous run, and the stage a matched record re-enters at is stated

specimens.label: The closing record, and what it leaves behind
specimens.subject: req #4471 · closing record

lines.text: Outcome: cleared every round · not selected · cohort: 4 finalists, 1 offer · reason class: cohort ranking — domain overlap
Standing: finalist · re-entry at the technical panel until 14 March · applies to any L4 requisition in Engineering
Sent with the decline: the cohort size, the class of reason, the re-entry stage and the date it runs to.
req #4471 reposted → 2 standings matched → both records enter the recruiter queue at the panel stage
Where the requisition closed unfunded rather than filled, the reason class reads funding withdrawn and the standing is recorded on the same terms.

specimens.reading: A ranking cannot be turned into a fault, and this does not try. It records what the ranking was and what the record is entitled to afterwards, so the outcome leaves something behind it.

perspectives.sees: A decline naming the cohort size, the class of reason, and the stage and date the record re-enters at.
perspectives.reads: The outcome was a ranking in a group of a stated size rather than a fault found in the rounds, and the record has a stated life after the decision.
perspectives.does: Applies again inside that date and enters at the stated stage, instead of starting the loop from the screen.

perspectives.sees: A required reason class and a cohort count on the closing record, and a queue where matched standings sit alongside new applications.
perspectives.reads: The outcome has to be classified before the requisition can be closed, and a comparison is one of the classes the taxonomy contains.
perspectives.does: Records the class, sends the cohort size and the re-entry date with the decline, and works the matched standings when a requisition at that level opens.

perspectives.sees: Two records arriving at the panel stage on a reposted requisition, each with the previous panel's scores attached.
perspectives.reads: The evidence the earlier loop produced is reusable up to the date on the standing; after that the record re-enters at the screen like any other.
perspectives.does: Runs the panel on the standing rather than the full loop, or lets the standing lapse where the level or the profile has moved.

items.title: Remove Career Gap Feature from Automated Ranking Models
items.content:
# Remove Career Gap Feature from Automated Ranking Models

Disable employment duration gap penalties in recruitment AI algorithms and screening models.

### Expected Effects
- mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias stops operating in the ranking model: continuity is no longer an input
- loop.employment_gap_penalty_loop loses the edge that closed it, because a gap can no longer widen the next gap

### Measurements
- `gap_candidate_screen_rate`
- `long_term_placement_success`
items.summary: Disable employment duration gap penalties in recruitment AI algorithms and screening models.
expected_effects: mech.employment_gap_downranking_bias stops operating in the ranking model: continuity is no longer an input
loop.employment_gap_penalty_loop loses the edge that closed it, because a gap can no longer widen the next gap

specimens.label: The same profile, with the feature removed

lines.text: Skills match: 91/100 · Domain match: 88/100
Continuity penalty: feature disabled
Final rank: 89/100 — advanced to recruiter queue
Model card updated: employment_gap removed from feature set, 14 March.

specimens.reading: The arithmetic is the whole intervention. The same person, the same work, above the threshold instead of below it.

perspectives.sees: A feature column in the training set, and the ranked order that shifts for every customer once it is removed.
perspectives.reads: The removal itself is one line in a feature list and a re-scoring run; the effect it is made for happens outside the platform, where there is no telemetry.
perspectives.does: Ships the change with the model card updated, and carries the support load from customers whose thresholds were tuned against the old distribution.

perspectives.sees: Profiles in the queue that the previous ranking placed below the review threshold.
perspectives.reads: The queue is longer and the screening capacity is the same; ranking decides reading order, not how many get read.
perspectives.does: Reads down the new order until capacity runs out, and the profiles below that line stay unread — for a reason that is no longer the gap.

perspectives.sees: A published model card naming the feature that was removed, in a market where the same feature ships enabled by default elsewhere.
perspectives.reads: One vendor removing it changes one vendor's ranking; what would hold it across the market is a rule about what an automated screen may read at all.
perspectives.does: Writes the requirement against what a vendor must publish and explain; what a customer switches on inside a configuration screen sits outside what any disclosure rule inspects.

items.title: Requirement changes versioned and sent to candidates in flight
items.content:
# Requirement changes versioned and sent to candidates in flight

The requisition carries a dated version of its requirements; when the team changes the stack, the level or the scope mid-search, everyone in flight is told what changed and which of their completed assessments still counts.

### Expected Effects
- mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition keeps operating — needs change — but stops being absorbed silently by the candidate
- Which specification an assessment was taken against becomes a recorded fact rather than a later reinterpretation

### Measurements
- `requisition_version_disclosure_rate`
- `assessments_revalued_without_notice`
items.summary: The requisition carries a dated version of its requirements; when the team changes the stack, the level or the scope mid-search, everyone in flight is told what changed and which of their completed assessments still counts.
expected_effects: mech.mid_process_role_requirement_redefinition keeps operating — needs change — but stops being absorbed silently by the candidate
Which specification an assessment was taken against becomes a recorded fact rather than a later reinterpretation

specimens.label: What goes out on the day the requirement moves

lines.text: req #5120 — requirements changed today, and what it means for your assessments
v3, 14 March: level moved from senior to staff; the service in scope changed from ingest to billing. v2 is archived and linked.
Your system design round was taken against v2 and still counts. The take-home was scoped to ingest and does not; we are not asking you to redo it, and it is not held against you.
If the new version is not the role you applied for, say so and we close the file with the reason recorded as ours.

specimens.reading: Teams' needs change mid-search and no policy stops that. What a version stops is the change being absorbed silently, so that work already done is quietly revalued against a specification the candidate never saw and a rejection is issued as though they had failed the new one. The cost is that the requisition has to admit which version each assessment was taken against.

perspectives.sees: A version bump on the requisition, and the list of candidates whose completed rounds it invalidates.
perspectives.reads: Changing the role mid-search has a cost that used to fall entirely on people outside the company; the list is that cost, itemised, at the moment the decision is made.
perspectives.does: Bumps the version deliberately, and decides per assessment whether it still counts rather than leaving it to the panel to reinterpret.

perspectives.sees: A generated notice listing what moved and which rounds survive, ready to send to everyone in flight.
perspectives.reads: The alternative was carrying the change silently and then explaining a rejection that came from it, which is the conversation this removes.
perspectives.does: Sends the notice the day the version moves, and closes files at the candidate's request with the reason recorded on the employer.

perspectives.sees: A dated diff of the role, and a line per assessment saying whether it still counts.
perspectives.reads: The ground moved, and it moved for reasons in the team's own plans — the work already submitted was not found wanting, it was scoped to a version that no longer exists.
perspectives.does: Decides whether the new version is worth continuing for, and keeps the rounds that still stand instead of starting over.

items.title: Requirements Drawn From the Team's Own Backlog
items.content:
# Requirements Drawn From the Team's Own Backlog

Draft the requisition's requirement list from the last two quarters of the team's actual work: every requirement the screen reads names a task it is required for, and anything without one is published in a separate section that is not screened on.

### Expected Effects
- mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs is split into two published lists: the screened list carries only requirements that name a task, and the wish sits in the section that is not screened on
- bar.requisition_approval_public_posting fixes a bar that states what each part of it is for: the requirement list is checkable against the team's own backlog rather than against the level in the grid
- loop.inflated_requirements_search_saturation_loop's entry point becomes an edit with a date — raising a requirement mid-search means adding a line with no task behind it

### Measurements
- `screened_requirement_count`
- `mid_search_requirement_edits`
- `screen_to_onsite_rate`
items.summary: Draft the requisition's requirement list from the last two quarters of the team's actual work: every requirement the screen reads names a task it is required for, and anything without one is published in a separate section that is not screened on.
expected_effects: mech.inflated_requisition_requirements_vs_actual_team_needs is split into two published lists: the screened list carries only requirements that name a task, and the wish sits in the section that is not screened on
bar.requisition_approval_public_posting fixes a bar that states what each part of it is for: the requirement list is checkable against the team's own backlog rather than against the level in the grid
loop.inflated_requirements_search_saturation_loop's entry point becomes an edit with a date — raising a requirement mid-search means adding a line with no task behind it

specimens.label: The requisition, with the list split
specimens.subject: Backend Engineer · Billing — requirements

lines.text: Screened on — Go, three years or more: billing endpoints and the report export, 40 of last quarter's 52 merged changes.
Screened on — SQL schema changes under load: the two migrations scheduled this quarter.
Not screened on, useful — Kubernetes, Terraform, Rust: no task in the last two quarters; the cluster is owned by the platform team.
Level: L4. The list was written from the backlog rather than carried over from the L5 search for this team.

specimens.reading: The same manager, the same worry about the ceiling. What changed is that a requirement now has to name a task, and the ones that cannot are still published — in the list nobody is screened against.

perspectives.sees: The requisition draft next to the last two quarters of merged work, and the requirements carried over from the previous search that now have to be matched to a task or moved.
perspectives.reads: The ceiling can still be written down, but it is written in a section the screen does not read; what is screened on is what the backlog can account for.
perspectives.does: Moves each unmatched line into the second section, and carries the risk that a requirement not screened on brings someone who has to learn it on the job.

perspectives.sees: Two lists in the requisition instead of one, and only the first is the screening standard.
perspectives.reads: What is movable is written down before the pipeline thins, rather than found by going back to the manager in week six.
perspectives.does: Screens against the first list, and passes the second one to candidates as a description of the work rather than as a bar.

perspectives.sees: A posting where each screened requirement names the work it is for, and a separate list marked as not screened on.
perspectives.reads: The bar is stated as the work rather than as a stack, so which lines the assessment runs against is readable before applying.
perspectives.does: Applies against the screened list, and reads the second section as description rather than as a threshold to clear.

items.title: Screening Note Bound to Observations and Disposition Codes
items.content:
# Screening Note Bound to Observations and Disposition Codes

Restrict the screening note to the requirement, what the record shows and the surface opened, and close it with a fixed disposition code — including a referral to levelling for profiles above the graded band.

### Expected Effects
- The forecast mech.experience_age_grading_mismatch is recorded as has no field to sit in: the note takes the requirement, what the record shows, and a disposition code
- mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation becomes checkable: the surface that was opened is recorded next to the note written from it, and the application form asks which surface that should be
- A profile above the graded band leaves bar.inbound_screening_triage with a routing code rather than a pass at screen

### Measurements
- `screening_note_field_completeness`
- `above_grid_referral_rate`
- `artifact_surface_recorded_rate`
items.summary: Restrict the screening note to the requirement, what the record shows and the surface opened, and close it with a fixed disposition code — including a referral to levelling for profiles above the graded band.
expected_effects: The forecast mech.experience_age_grading_mismatch is recorded as has no field to sit in: the note takes the requirement, what the record shows, and a disposition code
mech.portfolio_work_artifact_misinterpretation becomes checkable: the surface that was opened is recorded next to the note written from it, and the application form asks which surface that should be
A profile above the graded band leaves bar.inbound_screening_triage with a routing code rather than a pass at screen

specimens.label: The screening note, under the template
specimens.subject: Screen — Senior Payments Engineer, requisition R-2214

lines.text: Payments domain, service ownership. Graded L4, scoped 4–6 years.
Twelve years; three payment systems owned end to end. Above the graded band.

Profile page linked in the CV — three pinned forks. Artifact link from the application form — 40 commits to an upstream storage layer under another organisation, candidate named as owner of the rewrite.
above_grid — referred to levelling 2 April. Not closed at screen.
The template has no field for expected tenure, likely boredom or salary expectation.

specimens.reading: Two fields carry it. The surface actually opened is written next to the note written from it, and a profile above the band leaves a routing code rather than a pass.

perspectives.sees: A screening note with three fields — the requirement, what the record shows, the surface opened — and a fixed list of disposition codes to close it with.
perspectives.reads: The wording stays theirs; what may go into the note does not. A forecast about tenure has no field, and a profile above the band closes as a referral rather than as a pass.
perspectives.does: Records the surface actually opened next to the note written from it, and sends an above-band profile to levelling instead of closing it at the screen.

perspectives.sees: Two fields on the application form: the link where the work sits, and what their part in it is.
perspectives.reads: Which surface a screener opens is set on the form rather than discovered, so a profile page that does not show the work is no longer the only surface available.
perspectives.does: Links the commits and the repository rather than the account, and states the ownership in the field instead of leaving it in a CV line.

perspectives.sees: A referral route from screening into the levelling committee, and the volume that arrives on it once above-band stops being a pass.
perspectives.reads: The grid itself is unchanged; what changes is that the applications it excludes now reach the layer that maintains it.
perspectives.does: Sets the cadence the committee runs at and what it may decide, or does not — and where it does not, the referral is a code with nothing behind it.

items.title: Standardized Late-Stage Rejection Feedback Taxonomy
items.content:
# Standardized Late-Stage Rejection Feedback Taxonomy

Provide candidates reaching technical or panel stages with structured, rubric-based feedback categories rather than generic templates.

### Expected Effects
- The stage and the criterion behind a late rejection become part of what is sent
- mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority becomes checkable: a rubric that is reported has to exist before the round

### Measurements
- `informative_feedback_ratio`
- `interviewer_calibration_variance`
items.summary: Provide candidates reaching technical or panel stages with structured, rubric-based feedback categories rather than generic templates.
expected_effects: The stage and the criterion behind a late rejection become part of what is sent
mech.hidden_evaluation_rubric_or_undisclosed_priority becomes checkable: a rubric that is reported has to exist before the round

specimens.label: The rejection, rewritten to the taxonomy
specimens.subject: Outcome — technical panel

lines.text: Category: technical depth · Sub-category: complexity reasoning · Round: technical panel, exercise 2
What we saw: a correct quadratic solution where the panel was looking for the linear approach, reached without prompting.
What we did not assess: system design, collaboration, or domain knowledge — those rounds were positive or not reached.
Re-application window: six months, straight to the technical panel.

specimens.reading: The same decision, expressed as a category with a scope. Note the second line: saying what was not assessed is what stops a single round becoming a verdict on the person.

perspectives.sees: A panel recommendation, and a taxonomy that asks for a category, a round and a scope the recommendation does not contain.
perspectives.reads: The wording is theirs to write, but the content is not: a category can only be sent where the panel recorded one.
perspectives.does: Sends the structured note where the rubric was filled in, and the template where it was not.

perspectives.sees: A rubric field per round that has to be completed before the outcome is recorded, and the same fields from the other interviewers.
perspectives.reads: The cost is interviewer minutes booked before an outcome can be recorded; in return, two interviewers scoring one round differently becomes a number.
perspectives.does: Records the category and what the round did not assess, and calibrates where the panel's entries disagree.

perspectives.sees: A category, the round it came from, an explicit list of what was not assessed, and a re-application window.
perspectives.reads: One round stays a scored round rather than a verdict on the person, and the part of the process that was positive is stated rather than inferred.
perspectives.does: Works on the named category, and reapplies inside the stated window instead of treating the door as closed.

perspectives.sees: A proposed change to what is sent to rejected candidates: from a template that says nothing to a note that names a category.
perspectives.reads: Written feedback is consistent across every hire, which is what defensibility asks for, and is also a record that exists after the process ends.
perspectives.does: Defines which categories may be sent and which may not, and that definition is the boundary the recruiter writes inside.

items.title: Strict Take-Home Timebox & Blinded Evaluation Rubric
items.content:
# Strict Take-Home Timebox & Blinded Evaluation Rubric

Enforce strict 3-hour scope limits on take-homes, compensate candidates for extended samples, and grade submissions blind.

### Expected Effects
- mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry loses its asymmetry: the timebox binds the reviewer as well as the candidate
- Who wrote a submission stops being an input to how it is scored

### Measurements
- `take_home_completion_rate`
- `inter_rater_rubric_correlation`
items.summary: Enforce strict 3-hour scope limits on take-homes, compensate candidates for extended samples, and grade submissions blind.
expected_effects: mech.take_home_evaluation_fatigue_asymmetry loses its asymmetry: the timebox binds the reviewer as well as the candidate
Who wrote a submission stops being an input to how it is scored

specimens.label: The brief and the review record, both bounded
specimens.subject: Take-home — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Scope: one endpoint with persistence and tests. Hard timebox: 3 hours. Submit whatever you have at the three-hour mark.
Anything beyond three hours is paid at our contractor rate; tell us in advance if you want that option.
Review: submissions are anonymised before grading and scored against the published rubric by two reviewers, minimum 20 minutes each.

specimens.reading: Both halves of the asymmetry are addressed at once: the candidate hours are capped and the reviewer minutes have a floor. Capping only one side moves the problem rather than closing it.

perspectives.sees: A brief with a hard cap, submissions with the names stripped, and two review slots per submission on the team's calendar.
perspectives.reads: Reviewer minutes acquire a floor where they had none, and the loop is scheduled in advance rather than fitted around the week as it comes.
perspectives.does: Sets the scope so that three hours produces something gradable, and accepts the smaller sample as the evidence the hire is decided on.

perspectives.sees: A stated scope, a hard timebox, a rate for anything beyond it, and a published rubric the submission is graded against.
perspectives.reads: The hours are knowable before starting, and the grade is a scored artefact rather than an impression formed in a five-minute scan.
perspectives.does: Submits what exists at the three-hour mark instead of competing on hours, and weighs the task against the other processes in flight.

perspectives.sees: A request to pay a non-employee for an extended work sample, at a rate, on a contracting route.
perspectives.reads: Paying for a sample is a procurement and classification question before it is a hiring one; an unpaid task raises neither.
perspectives.does: Defines the rate and the route, or does not — and where it does not, only the timebox half of the intervention ships.

items.title: Upfront Compensation Band Disclosure
items.content:
# Upfront Compensation Band Disclosure

Publish verified salary and equity bands directly in job descriptions or disclose them prior to scheduling technical interview rounds.

### Expected Effects
- mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy has nothing to operate on: the band is stated before the candidate is asked for a number
- bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation becomes arithmetic rather than a negotiation about whether a band exists

### Measurements
- `late_stage_compensation_drop_rate`
- `screen_to_offer_band_agreement_rate`
items.summary: Publish verified salary and equity bands directly in job descriptions or disclose them prior to scheduling technical interview rounds.
expected_effects: mech.unstated_compensation_band_discrepancy has nothing to operate on: the band is stated before the candidate is asked for a number
bar.compensation_levelling_reconciliation becomes arithmetic rather than a negotiation about whether a band exists

specimens.label: The posting with the band in it
specimens.subject: Senior Backend Engineer · Payments

lines.text: Level: L4 · Base band: 68,000–79,000 · Equity: 0.02–0.04% · Band verified by finance on 3 March.
We will not ask for your expectations before showing you this number.
If your expectation sits above the band, tell us at the screen and we will say honestly whether the level can move.

specimens.reading: Every branch of the compensation bind needs the candidate to speak first. Publishing the number removes the asymmetry the bind is built on.

perspectives.sees: A posting draft with a band in it, and the same band readable by everyone already employed at that level.
perspectives.reads: Publishing fixes a number that was previously settled per candidate, and makes internal pay spread visible in a document anyone can open.
perspectives.does: Requires the band to be verified by finance before the posting goes live, which adds an approval step to publishing a role.

perspectives.sees: The band as a published line in the requisition, available before the screening call rather than after the panel.
perspectives.reads: The expectation question is no longer the filter: a candidate above the band says so at the screen, where the process has cost nobody five rounds.
perspectives.does: Opens the screen with the number, and routes a mismatch into the levelling question instead of carrying it to the offer stage.

perspectives.sees: The band and the level in the posting, dated and attributed, before any unpaid hours are committed.
perspectives.reads: The one number the whole process is arranged around is available before entering it, so applying becomes a decision about a known range.
perspectives.does: Applies or does not, and where the expectation sits above the band, raises it at the screen instead of at the offer.

perspectives.sees: Postings carrying a band in covered jurisdictions, and postings carrying one elsewhere because the practice spread.
perspectives.reads: Compliance is checkable against the text of the posting; the level a candidate is actually assessed at sits outside what any current disclosure rule reaches.
perspectives.does: Sets the requirement on the posting, the one artefact an inspection can check; the levelling decision has no comparable artefact for a rule to attach to.
